children: The promoters of Pricol announced the sale of their entire stake of 38.5 per cent in Pricol Autotech to Warburg Pincus on November 13 (Friday). The stock fell 17.9 per cent on Monday and is now down 15 per cent from November 13. Here we look at what the deal means for investors.

Pricol has three verticals namely, DICVS, ACFMS and P3L. Details of the business and fundamentals can be found in our earlier article dated August 30. The DICVS vertical, where Pricol manufactures instrument clusters, is set to be spun off into Pricol Autotech. Existing shareholders of Pricol, including promoters who hold 38.5 per cent, will receive one share of Pricol Autotech (will be listed) for every share in Pricol. The demerger will be completed after regulatory clearances.

Warburg Pincus is buying the post-demerger stake of promoters in Pricol Autotech for ₹1,663 crore, which values the DICVS vertical (60 per cent of Pricol’s revenue) at roughly ₹4,300 crore. This valuation is lower than that built in the market-cap of Pricol, before the deal was made public. Apportioning the pre-deal market-cap based on revenue indicates that the market was valuing the DICVS business at about ₹5,450 crore (₹9,112 crore x 60 per cent). Broadly adjusting for this difference of ₹1,150 crore, Pricol trades at a market-cap of ₹7,750 crore today. P/E of the stock is now 26.7x, down from 31.4x on November 13, before the deal was announced.

Promoters’ rationale for the sale is as follows. Instrument clusters in cars are becoming more complex and integrate (through numerous sensors) vehicle information, navigation, infotainment, climate control and ADAS features — all-in-one touch screen interface. What Pricol sells currently are simpler and a foray into the more sophisticated ones would involve massive infusion of capital — the kind promoters are unable to mobilise. Warburg Pincus has the financial might and a global network to strike technology partnerships (organic/ inorganic) — explaining the stake sale.

That said, business is growing well. In H1 FY27, revenue and profit grew 29 per cent and 33 per cent — and is poised to post earnings growth of about 20 per cent CAGR over FY26-28, per our estimates. Capex of ₹700-800 crore at seven facilities over FY27-28 is underway, across the three verticals. When these facilities mature, the ACFMS and P3L verticals, which contributed about ₹1,600 crore of revenue in FY26, are expected to expand to ₹4,000 crore. Earnings for the Warburg Pincus-controlled DICVS vertical can be higher, given more complex products and higher margins.
Promoters have assured continuity of business plans and retention of senior management. Customers were consulted and they, too, are on board with the deal.

We had written a positive note on Pricol in August 2025 when it was trading at ₹460 and advised investors to take some gains off the table in August 2026, when its price grew to ₹770 at a P/E of 35x. Considering the above growth drivers, investors holding the stock can continue to do so.

title: Warburg Pincus buys stake in Pricol Autotech: What should investors do?
